items.subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
items.stimulus: Seismologist Rena Okafor has spent a decade monitoring the Tarsin Fault, which typically releases strain through thousands of tremors too faint for nearby residents to feel. The magnitude 6.1 earthquake that struck the fault in 2019 was therefore a striking departure from its usual behavior. ______ in the forty years of records preceding that event, no tremor on the fault had exceeded magnitude 3.5.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence before the blank says the 2019 quake was a striking departure from the fault's usual behavior. The sentence after it backs up that claim: for forty years nothing larger than magnitude 3.5 had happened, which is exactly why a 6.1 counts as an outlier. The second sentence strengthens the first rather than adding a separate point, so you need an emphasis word. 'Indeed' is that word.

A.why: You saw the gap between a 6.1 quake and tremors under 3.5 and read it as a contrast. The small tremors don't argue against the main claim, though. They are the reason the 2019 quake counts as a departure, so the second sentence supports the first.

C.why: You treated the second sentence as a result of the first. The forty quiet years came before the 2019 quake, so they can't be its consequence. They are evidence for calling it a departure.

D.why: 'Instead' means one thing is taking the place of another. Nothing is being replaced here. The second sentence confirms the first.

items.subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
items.stimulus: Before a revised coastal chart is released, cartographers at the national hydrographic office check it against three independent sources. They start by comparing every depth figure on the draft with the most recent sonar surveys of the seabed. ______ they cross-reference each lighthouse, buoy, and beacon against the coast guard's current registry of navigational aids. Lastly, they review reports submitted by ship captains of hazards not yet charted.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The passage describes three separate checks, and the words 'start by' and 'Lastly' mark the first and third. The sentence after the blank gives the second check, which is a new item of the same kind as the first. That is simple addition, so 'In addition' is correct.

A.why: You noticed the umbrella phrase 'three independent sources' and expected an example. But the sentence just before the blank is already one specific check. The registry check isn't an instance of the sonar comparison. It is a separate check that comes next.

B.why: 'Even so' introduces something that goes against what came before. The registry check doesn't undercut the sonar comparison. It is simply the next step in the same procedure.

D.why: You read the second check as a result of the first. Checking depth figures doesn't lead to checking lighthouses and buoys. The two are independent steps in a planned sequence.

items.subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
items.stimulus: To slow drivers on Harlow Avenue, traffic engineer Lucía Brandt recommended that the city narrow the street from four lanes to two and widen its sidewalks. The city council did not merely approve her proposal. ______ it voted to close two blocks of the avenue to cars altogether, turning them into a pedestrian plaza lined with benches and trees.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence before the blank says the council did more than approve Brandt's proposal. The sentence after it says how much more: it closed two blocks to cars entirely. The second sentence keeps the same point and makes it stronger, and 'In fact' is the word for that kind of intensification.

A.why: The phrase 'did not merely approve' sounds negative, so you expected a reversal. The council didn't turn against Brandt's idea, though. It went further in the same direction. A sentence that goes beyond the first one doesn't contradict it.

B.why: 'Otherwise' introduces what would happen if something else were not true. The plaza vote isn't a hypothetical alternative. It is what the council actually did.

C.why: 'For instance' introduces one example drawn from a larger group. The passage doesn't set up a group of actions to sample from. The plaza vote is the single action that shows how far the council went.

items.subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
items.stimulus: Excavations at the Iron Age hillfort of Dun Carrach suggest that its massive earthen ramparts served more than one purpose. Charred timber reinforcements buried within the walls indicate that they were designed to withstand a sustained attack. ______ grain pits cut into the inner face of the ramparts show that the walls also functioned as protected storage for the settlement's harvest.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says the ramparts had more than one purpose. The second gives one purpose, defense. The sentence after the blank gives a separate, parallel one, storage, and even includes the word 'also'. A new item of the same kind calls for an addition word, so 'Additionally' is correct.

A.why: Defense and storage sound like very different uses, and that surface difference made you reach for a contrast. The storage finding doesn't argue against the defensive function. Both support the claim that the walls had more than one purpose.

C.why: You connected the grain pits to 'more than one purpose' and read them as an example. But the sentence right before the blank is about defense, and storage isn't an example of defense. It is a second purpose added next to the first.

D.why: You treated storage as a result of the timber reinforcements. Nothing in the passage says the defensive design caused the grain pits. They are separate pieces of evidence for separate uses.

items.subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
items.stimulus: Although the yellow prawn-goby is a capable swimmer, researchers studying the fish in the Red Sea found that it almost never strays from the burrow it shares with a nearly blind snapping shrimp. ______ across more than 300 hours of underwater video, tagged gobies spent over 95 percent of their time within five centimeters of a burrow entrance.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence before the blank says the goby almost never strays from its burrow. The sentence after the blank supports that claim with precise numbers: more than 95 percent of its time spent within five centimeters of the entrance. Evidence that confirms and sharpens the same point calls for 'Indeed'.

A.why: You responded to the phrase 'capable swimmer' and expected something against it. That concession is already dealt with inside the first sentence. The video data supports the main claim that the fish stays near its burrow.

B.why: You read the video data as a result of the goby's behavior. The data is the evidence researchers used to establish that behavior. It confirms the claim rather than following from it.

D.why: 'Alternatively' offers a different option or explanation. The video findings aren't an alternative to the claim. They support it directly.

items.subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
items.stimulus: Fossilized leaves give paleobotanists far more than a record of which plants grew where. The density of stomata, the tiny pores on a leaf's surface, can be used to estimate how much carbon dioxide the ancient atmosphere contained. ______ the shape of a leaf's edges, whether smooth or toothed, helps researchers infer the average annual temperature of the climate in which the plant lived.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says fossil leaves reveal more than where plants grew. Stomatal density is one thing they reveal, carbon dioxide levels. Leaf-edge shape is a second, separate thing, temperature. Adding a new point of the same kind calls for 'Moreover'.

B.why: 'For instance' would make leaf-edge shape an example of the idea just before the blank, estimating carbon dioxide. It is a different clue about a different climate variable. It is added to the stomata point, not drawn from it.

C.why: The switch from pores and carbon dioxide to edges and temperature seemed like a shift in direction, so you picked a contrast word. The two findings don't pull against each other. Both support the claim that fossil leaves reveal more than location.

D.why: You treated the leaf-edge method as a consequence of the stomata method. One technique doesn't lead to the other. They are independent tools listed side by side.

items.subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
items.stimulus: In a three-year trial, farmers in central Iowa planted crimson clover between rows of harvested corn each fall. Over the winter, the clover's dense roots held the soil in place during heavy rains, cutting erosion on the test fields by nearly half. ______ because clover draws nitrogen from the air and fixes it in the soil, the same fields required about 30 percent less fertilizer the following spring.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence before the blank gives one benefit of the clover, less erosion. The sentence after it gives a second, separate benefit, less need for fertilizer, which works through a different mechanism. Both point the same way, so you need an addition word, and 'In addition' is correct.

A.why: You may have sensed a change in direction when the passage moved from soil to nitrogen. Both sentences describe advantages of planting clover, though, so nothing is contradicted.

C.why: Less fertilizer isn't an example of reduced erosion. It is a different benefit with its own cause, placed next to the first one.

D.why: 'Instead' means the second benefit replaces the first. The erosion benefit still holds. The fertilizer savings add to it.

items.subtype_name: Adding another point, or doubling down (In addition / Moreover / Indeed)
items.stimulus: Astronomers have generally expected comets to lose most of their surface ice after a few hundred passes near the Sun, fading into dim, inactive bodies. Comet Halvorsen-4, however, remains unusually active even though it has completed thousands of such orbits. ______ when it swung past the Sun last spring, its glowing coma outshone that of every other comet observed that year.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The sentence before the blank says Halvorsen-4 is still unusually active. The sentence after it gives vivid support: its coma outshone every other comet that year. This strengthens the same claim instead of adding a new one or reversing it, so 'Indeed' is correct.

A.why: The passage already contains 'however' and 'even though', so you expected another reversal. But the bright coma doesn't go against the comet's unusual activity. It confirms it. The contrast with general expectations is already dealt with in the sentence before the blank.

B.why: 'Alternatively' offers another possibility. The bright coma isn't a competing explanation or option. It is evidence for the claim just made.

C.why: You compared the bright coma with the 'dim, inactive bodies' mentioned earlier. The sentence before the blank already says Halvorsen-4 is the exception. The coma supports that point rather than contrasting with it.

items.subtype_name: Solve a given system, where one variable is already isolated
items.stimulus:
An urban planning student checks this system from a zoning worksheet.

$y = 3x$

$x + y = 20$
items.stem: The solution to the given system of equations is $(x, y)$. What is the value of $y$?
items.explanation: The first equation already gives $y$ in terms of $x$. Substitute $3x$ for $y$ in the second equation: $x + 3x = 20$, so $4x = 20$ and $x = 5$. Then put this back into $y = 3x$ to get $y = 3(5) = 15$.

A.why: You solved for $x = 5$ correctly and then stopped. The question asks for $y$, so you still need to substitute back into $y = 3x$.

B.why: You combined $x + 3x$ as $2x$, which gives $x = 10$. The two terms add to $4x$.

D.why: $20$ is the value of $x + y$ given in the second equation. It is not the value of $y$ alone.

items.subtype_name: Solve a given system, where one variable is already isolated
items.stimulus:
A marine biology student uses this system in a lab exercise.

$x = 2y - 1$

$3x + y = 32$
items.stem: The solution to the given system of equations is $(x, y)$. What is the value of $x$?
items.explanation: Substitute $2y - 1$ for $x$ in the second equation: $3(2y - 1) + y = 32$, so $6y - 3 + y = 32$, $7y = 35$ and $y = 5$. Then $x = 2(5) - 1 = 9$.

A.why: $5$ is the value of $y$, the first variable you find. The question asks for $x$, so substitute $y = 5$ into $x = 2y - 1$.

C.why: You dropped the coefficient 3 and wrote $(2y - 1) + y = 32$, which gives $y = 11$ and $x = 21$.

D.why: $35$ is the value of $7y$ partway through the work. You still need to divide by 7 and then substitute back to find $x$.

items.stimulus:
An archaeology student sets up this system while cataloguing a site.

$y = x + 4$

$2x + y = 19$
items.stem: What is the solution $(x, y)$ to the given system of equations?
items.explanation: Substitute $x + 4$ for $y$ in the second equation: $2x + x + 4 = 19$, so $3x = 15$ and $x = 5$. Then $y = 5 + 4 = 9$. The pair $(5, 9)$ satisfies both equations.

D.why: You found the right values but swapped them. The ordered pair lists $x$ first, and $x = 5$.

items.stimulus:
Astronomers tracked the fading of a supernova after its peak brightness. The table shows its relative brightness $B$, in arbitrary units, $t$ days after the peak. The brightness falls by the same factor over each equal time interval.

D.why: This is a linear model built from the first two rows. It gives 0 at $t = 60$ instead of 100, because the brightness drops by a constant factor, not a constant amount.

items.subtype_name: Write or use an exponential growth or decay model
items.stimulus: A civil engineering firm counted an average of 25,000 vehicles per day crossing a river bridge in 2024. For its maintenance plan, the firm predicts that the average daily traffic will increase by 4% each year after 2024.

items.subtype_name: Write or use an exponential growth or decay model
items.stimulus: Drypoint plates in printmaking wear down as prints are pulled from them. A printmaking studio gives a new plate a quality score of 100. Its model says that each print reduces the score by 10% of the score just before that print.
items.stem: According to the model, after which print does the plate's quality score first fall below 50?
items.explanation: After $n$ prints, the score is $100(0.9)^{n}$. After the 6th print it is $100(0.9)^{6} \approx 53.1$, which is still above 50. After the 7th print it is $100(0.9)^{7} \approx 47.8$. So the 7th print is the first one that brings the score below 50.

B.why: You subtracted 10 points per print, which is a linear model, and solved $100 - 10n = 50$. Each 10% is taken from a smaller score, so the losses shrink and the score falls more slowly.

C.why: After the 6th print the score is about 53.1, which is not yet below 50. That is the last print that keeps the score above 50, not the first one that drops it below.

items.subtype_name: Result of what came before (Thus / Hence / For this reason / As such)

items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The earlier sentences describe how iron frames let strings be struck harder. The last sentence gives the outcome: composers wrote louder music. You can put 'so' between them, which makes this a cause-and-effect relationship, and 'As a result' signals it.

D.why: You read a contrast where there is none. Louder music follows naturally from strings that can be struck harder. It does not go against that point.

items.stimulus: When a regional hospital raised wages for its night-shift nurses by 15 percent, far fewer of them left to work for competing employers over the following year. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Fewer nurses left, so fewer replacements were needed, so the hospital spent less on hiring and training them. 'Offset the cost of the raise' confirms that the spending went down. 'Reduce' fits the chain exactly.

B.why: You picked a verb that goes in the right general direction but acts on the wrong thing. Keeping staff changes how much the hospital spends, not whether the spending is hidden.

items.stimulus: Waterlogged peat bogs contain very little oxygen, and the bacteria and fungi that break down organic matter need oxygen to thrive. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: With no oxygen, the organisms that cause decay cannot thrive, so buried objects do not rot. Objects that do not rot are 'preserved,' which also fits the contrast with things that 'would have rotted away.'

B.why: You reversed the chain. Low oxygen stops decay, so the objects survive. They are not destroyed.

D.why: You matched the museum setting instead of the causal logic. The bog's chemistry affects whether the objects decay, not whether anyone exhibits them.
